title: Introduce telemetry-aware prompt-delta fusion CI adapter
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Add a CI adapter that fuses time-series telemetry with prompt-set delta signals so regressions can be contextualized by recent infra or model telemetry. Enables softer gating when external noise is detected and recommends prioritized probe replays.
description:
Motivation: We observed several spurious prompt-set CI failures that correlated with infrastructure noise (GPU preemptions, model cache warmups) and short-lived traffic pattern changes. Existing gates treat prompt-delta signals in isolation which leads to noisy alerts and flakey CI. This PR introduces a telemetry-aware "diff-fusion" CI adapter that ingests lightweight time-series signals alongside prompt regression deltas and produces a contextualized decision (pass/soft-fail/hard-fail) plus a ranked remediation suggestion list.

Design summary: The adapter: 1) pulls recent telemetry slices (latency p95, GPU context switches, KV cache hit-rate, model-variant rollouts) from the eval harness telemetry API; 2) computes a normalized noise score and a correlation vector between telemetry features and prompt deltas; 3) applies a configurable fusion policy to attenuate or escalate regressions (soft-fail -> create backfill job / hard-fail -> block merge); 4) emits a compact explainable payload to CI logs and the failure reporter. The fusion policy is declarative and lives in eval_harness/config/default_gates.yaml so SRE/Product can tune thresholds without code changes.

Commits: - c1a4d8b: add telemetry ingestion and lightweight TS utils (metrics/telemetry_ingest.py, utils/time_series.py) - b2f3a21: implement fusion adapter and policy engine (ci/adapters/telemetry_diff_fusion.py) - 9e7d4ff: hook adapter into eval CI workflow and add gating behavior (infra/ci/workflows/eval-ci.yaml) - 4a0b6cc: tests + example telemetry probe + docs (tests/test_telemetry_diff.py, examples/telemetry_probe_example.json, docs/ci/telemetry-fusion.md) - d5f8e33: prompt snapshotter integration to link failing prompts to recent telemetry windows (hooks/prompt_snapshotter.py)

Changed areas (high level): - New CI adapter under eval_harness/ci/adapters. The adapter is intentionally lightweight: it requests at most 5m windows and falls back to a conservative default if telemetry is unavailable. - New telemetry ingestion helpers; they include a pluggable backend interface with an in-process memory cache to avoid CI timeouts. - Workflow changes to wire the adapter into the existing eval CI path; the default behavior is opt-in via gate config. - Docs and examples demonstrating how to interpret the fusion score and common tuning recipes for latency vs. model-quality tradeoffs.

Testing and CI: Unit tests cover the fusion heuristics and the correlation scorer. An integration smoke test runs the adapter against a recorded telemetry fixture to ensure deterministic outcomes. CI run initially flagged a flakey test due to time window boundary handling; fixed by normalizing timestamps to UTC and adding a small jitter tolerance. Final CI: build/pylint/pytest all green; ephemeral pipeline rerun showed consistent pass.

Review conversation highlights: - Ethan Zhao (reviewer): "Nice work — the policy DSL is clear. One concern: how do we avoid masking true regressions if telemetry is maliciously noisy?" Author reply (Maya): "We added a mandatory minimum regression magnitude override in the policy (min_delta_absolute) — telemetry can only downgrade severity, not hide a large absolute regression. Documented in default_gates.yaml." - Priya Kapoor: "Add more unit tests for correlation edge-cases, and verify behavior when telemetry API returns sparse points." Author: "Added three targeted tests and a fallback code path that marks telemetry as 'sparse' and pushes adapter to conservative mode." - Liam O'Rourke: "Consider emitting a compact JSON blob to the trace exporter so dashboards can surface fusion decisions." Author: "Added an export hook and an example dashboard snippet in docs/ci/telemetry-fusion.md."

Behavioral notes and operator guidance: - Default policy is turned off for existing repositories to avoid surprise behavior; teams can opt in per-prompt-set in config. - When fusion outputs 'soft-fail' the CI posts a comment with suggested remediation: rerun with isolated shard, schedule backfill, or mark noisy telemetry as investigation item. - Hard-fail remains reserved for high-confidence deltas where telemetry correlation is low and variance is within historical norms.

Backward compatibility and risk: The adapter is additive and respects current eval gateway contracts. It does not change existing scoring metrics; it only post-processes the delta decision. The main risk is over-tuning the fusion policy; to mitigate we ship conservative defaults and added a new dashboard that surfaces historical fusion decisions for manual review.

Merge notes: Squash-merged after approvals from Ethan and Priya. Changelog entry added to release notes; docs published to the internal docs site. Next steps: 1) run a small canary where the adapter is opt-in for 10 teams; 2) collect telemetry-fusion metrics (attenuated_count, exacerbated_count, ignored_count) and review after 2 weeks.
